prompt: Stage 2-5, level 5 with 26 gold at 94 HP. Your board has no 2-stars and nothing in the shop pairs. Three other players have clearly stronger stage-2 boards. You lost the last two fights for 4 HP each. What is your plan through stage 2?

options.label: Accept the losses: buy nothing, bank toward 50, take the loss-streak gold, and plan the first real spend at 3-2
Roll 10 gold now for pairs so you stop losing
Level to 6 early to fit more units and win a round

explanation:
Stage 2 losses cost 2 to 4 HP each. At 94 HP you can lose every remaining stage-2 fight and enter 3-1 above 80. Meanwhile a loss streak pays up to 3 gold a round on top of interest, so a deliberate open-fort gets you to 50 gold by 3-1 with the whole lobby ahead of you on board and behind you on econ. HP spent in stage 2 is the cheapest HP in the game; HP spent in stage 4 costs 12 a fight.

Rolling ten gold at level 5 to stop losing 4-HP fights is paying interest to avoid a cost that is smaller than the interest. Leveling to 6 at 2-5 to win one round breaks the streak, delays the 50, and buys a unit slot you have nothing good to put in. The exit condition of this plan is fixed now: at 3-2 you have the augment, ~50 gold, and you spend.
principle: HP is cheapest in stage 2: a planned loss streak converts it into gold at the best rate you will ever get.
commonMistake: Rolling in stage 2 to stop a loss streak that is paying you, because losing feels bad.
